channel.title: WEBSPACEAI Journal
channel.description: Research analyses and company policy explainers.

item.title: GRPO efficiency starts before the kernel
item.description: A practical investigation of sparse rewards, loss normalization, and what a faster training step actually proves.

item.title: A coding agent is a system, not a score
item.description: How to compare coding agents without confusing model quality, scaffolding, test contamination, and retry budget.

item.title: Robot foundation models need a data contract
item.description: What GR00T and π₀ teach us about the gap between a general model and a reliable policy on a particular robot.

item.title: A map should know what it does not know
item.description: A proposed architecture for LiDAR–camera mapping that keeps geometric confidence separate from semantic guesses.

item.title: RAG should earn the right to answer
item.description: A claim-level design for retrieval, contradiction handling, citations, and useful abstention.

item.title: Prompt injection is a permission problem too
item.description: Why an agent’s ability to read a document should not grant that document authority to authorize an action.

item.title: Long context has a memory budget
item.description: A worked KV-cache calculation, and why FlashAttention, GQA, and PagedAttention solve different problems.

item.title: Inside the WEBSPACEAI Trust Center
item.description: A reader’s guide to the policy directory, its cross-references, and the questions the documents are intended to answer.

item.title: How our safety risk levels work
item.description: The published AI Safety Framework describes four risk levels. Here is how to read the escalation and release controls without confusing a policy with a test result.
